newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to keep aluminium import tariff - EAA chairman.
newsitem.headline: EU to keep aluminium import tariff - EAA chairman.

text.p: A six percent European Union tariff on imports of primary aluminium will be maintained, said Bernard Legrand, Chairman of the European Aluminium Association.
"We'll keep the tariff in place for the time being," Legrand said in response to a question at the group's annual news conference.
"The objective is not to protect an obsolete industry," he stressed, adding that two-thirds of European smelters were less than 25 years old following a painful restructuring.
Legrand said the duty allowed European aluminium producers to compete against cheap imports from Russia and Mideast Gulf producers.
It also compensated European producers for fluctuations of the dollar - the currency for aluminium trade - as small changes in exchange rates resulted in profit or loss for European smelters.
But Richard Gaunt of Alcan told Reuters the EU imported 55 percent of its primary aluminium and the duty distorted trade and penalised the EU manufacturing industry with higher costs.
"The six percent tariff should be phased out," he said, noting that the EU was the only major trading bloc to maintain an aluminium import tariff. -Peter Blackburn Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
